macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stock futures rebound as oil retreats and investors weigh Iran tensions
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures edged higher after oil prices steadied, even as fresh U.S. strikes on Iran kept geopolitical risk elevated and threatened to prolong market volatility. Reuters said the move reflected investors balancing safer energy prices against renewed Middle East uncertainty.

items.title: Fed's Williams downplays risk of a sustained energy-price shock
items.summary: New York Fed President John Williams said he was not expecting a sustained surge in energy prices despite the renewed conflict in the Middle East. The comment helped temper concerns that higher oil prices would force a more hawkish policy response.

items.title: Wall Street futures and global markets supported by retreat in oil prices
items.summary: Markets recovered as oil prices eased, with Reuters reporting that investors were weighing the impact of the U.S.-Iran conflict against broader risk sentiment. The tone across equities was firmer even as geopolitical uncertainty remained a key driver.

items.title: PepsiCo beats quarterly revenue estimates on stronger snack and zero-sugar soda demand
items.summary: PepsiCo reported second-quarter revenue above Wall Street expectations, citing improving demand for salty snacks in the U.S. and resilient demand for zero-sugar sodas. The result was one of the notable company earnings updates in the past day.

items.title: U.S. labor market data stays resilient despite slower job growth
items.summary: Weekly jobless claims fell and were cited as evidence that the labor market remained in a slow-hire, slow-fire pattern. MarketWatch also highlighted recent jobs data showing softer hiring, which reinforced expectations that the Fed may remain cautious.

items.title: US markets face renewed funding pressure as leverage rises
items.summary: Reuters reported that equity funding markets remain stretched, with near-record stock prices and heavy demand for leverage in popular technology shares increasing vulnerability. The note flagged tighter financing conditions as a risk for the rally.

items.title: China producer inflation accelerates to near four-year high
items.summary: Reuters reported that China’s producer price inflation rose for a fourth straight month in June to its highest level since July 2022, while consumer prices also increased. The data pointed to persistent cost pressure for manufacturers.

items.title: Asia-Pacific markets mixed; Japanese equities pressured while oil-linked shares gained
items.summary: MarketScreener reported that Australian shares wobbled as Fed caution offset oil-price optimism, while Japan’s Topix rose on the oil drop and the Nikkei lagged on tech weakness. The regional picture remained uneven across sectors.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rises above $63K as macro tailwinds lift risk appetite
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed above $63,000 in the latest session, with easing oil prices and broader risk-on sentiment supporting the move. Other market feeds also show BTC trading in the low-$60K range after a volatile 24 hours.

items.title: Crypto markets see heavy liquidations as volatility persists
items.summary: Market reports show roughly $554 million in crypto liquidations over the past 24 hours, with short positions making up the majority. That suggests traders were caught offside by the rebound in prices.

items.title: Bitcoin ETF flows remain mixed while ether and solana products attract demand
items.summary: Recent market coverage says ether and solana products have seen inflows, while bitcoin outflows exceeded $290 million. This points to a rotation away from BTC and toward alternative crypto funds.

items.title: Paul Grewal exits Coinbase legal leadership before key CLARITY vote
items.summary: crypto.news reports that Coinbase legal chief Paul Grewal is leaving his role just ahead of a crucial CLARITY Act vote. The timing makes the departure notable because the bill is a major focus for U.S. crypto regulation.

items.title: Senate races toward key crypto market-structure vote
items.summary: Coverage highlights renewed attention on the CLARITY Act and related Senate action, with debate centered on developer protections and broader crypto market structure rules. The latest reporting frames this as one of the most important regulatory developments in the sector.

items.title: Trump faces fresh CLARITY Act test amid Washington crypto push
items.summary: crypto.news says Trump is facing another CLARITY Act test as the Senate moves toward a key vote. The story underscores how closely U.S. crypto policy is tied to the current legislative calendar.

items.title: Hong Kong tightens crypto platform security rules
items.summary: crypto.news reports that Hong Kong's securities regulator is forcing crypto platforms to move away from SMS authentication. The change is part of a broader push to improve exchange security and reduce account-takeover risk.

items.title: Bitdeer opens new Nevada factory aimed at Bitcoin mining expansion
items.summary: Bitdeer unveiled a $36 million Nevada factory, signaling continued investment in Bitcoin mining infrastructure. The project adds to ongoing industry efforts to scale hardware and operations.

items.title: Ethereum Foundation says AI still fails at finding real bugs
items.summary: The Ethereum Foundation released a note arguing that AI tools still struggle to identify genuine software bugs reliably. The development is notable for developers tracking where AI can and cannot help with blockchain security.

items.title: XRP gains after SWIFT-linked banking payments update
items.summary: crypto.news says XRP rose as SWIFT tapped Ripple-linked banks for blockchain payments. The move is another sign of traditional-finance experimentation with blockchain-based settlement rails.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox restructuring leads to layoffs and studio divestments
items.summary: Microsoft is reportedly making major cuts in its gaming division, including layoffs and the sale of four Xbox studios. The shake-up is one of the biggest industry stories in the last day and signals a broader restructuring of Xbox's first-party strategy.

items.title: Sony says physical PlayStation game discs are ending for new titles
items.summary: Sony has clarified that production of physical game discs for new PlayStation titles will end in January 2028, after which new games will be digital-only. The move marks another major step away from physical media in console gaming.

items.title: Nintendo will stop selling the original Switch in Europe next year
items.summary: Nintendo has quietly confirmed that the original Switch family will no longer be sold to retailers in Europe beginning in mid-February 2027. The change suggests Nintendo is continuing to phase out the older hardware line.

items.title: Capcom moves up the release of Onimusha: Way of the Sword
items.summary: Capcom has advanced the launch of Onimusha: Way of the Sword to September 4, moving it up from the previously planned September 25 date. The new date places it in a crowded late-year release window.

items.title: EA names new leadership after its private acquisition
items.summary: Electronic Arts has appointed a new Chief Studios Officer and Chief Operating Officer following completion of its US$55 billion private acquisition. The leadership changes are part of a significant post-deal corporate reset.

items.title: Nintendo reports strong sales for Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream
items.summary: Nintendo said sales of Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream have exceeded 8 million units. The update adds to the company's recent run of strong software performance.

items.title: Nintendo quarterly profit rises sharply on game sales and tariff repayment
items.summary: Nintendo reported quarterly profit growth of 150.5%, driven by strong game sales and a US$300 million tariff repayment from the U.S. government. The results point to a strong financial period for the company.

items.title: Mistfall Hunter reaches 1 million players in its first week
items.summary: The fantasy extraction RPG Mistfall Hunter has reportedly surpassed 1 million players in its launch week. The milestone suggests strong early interest in the new release.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed director returns after five years at EA Motive
items.summary: Former Assassin’s Creed game director Eric Baptizat is returning to the franchise after a five-year stint at EA's Motive Studio. The move is a notable personnel development for Ubisoft's long-running series.

items.title: Epic Games settles leak lawsuit involving former Fortnite contractor
items.summary: Epic Games has settled its lawsuit against former contractor Hayden Cohen, who was accused of leaking confidential Fortnite collaboration plans. The company also dropped monetary claims in the dispute.
